prompt.zh-TW: 初陽貿易今年營業收入 {{money:vars.revenue}}，年底應收帳款 {{money:vars.ar}}（週轉率見上表）。換算下來，平均收現日數從去年的 {{number:vars.lastDays|digits=2,unit=day}} 變成今年的 {{number:vars.thisDays|digits=2,unit=day}}，兩年的營業收入差不多。哪一個判讀最合理？
prompt.en: First Light Trading had revenue of {{money:vars.revenue}} this year and trade receivables of {{money:vars.ar}} at year end (turnover in the table above). Converted to days, the average collection period went from {{number:vars.lastDays|digits=2,unit=day}} last year to {{number:vars.thisDays|digits=2,unit=day}} this year, with revenue about the same in both years. Which reading is most reasonable?

text.zh-TW: 客戶付款變慢，更多資金押在應收帳款上，現金壓力變大
text.en: Customers are paying more slowly, more money is tied up in receivables and cash pressure is rising

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。營收沒變、天數變長，就是同樣的生意收錢收得更慢；接下來該檢查收款政策，以及有沒有收不回來的帳。
feedback.en: That’s right. With revenue unchanged, longer days simply mean the same sales are being collected more slowly; the next step is to review the collection policy and check for bad debts.

text.zh-TW: 收現日數變長代表客戶變多、生意變好
text.en: A longer collection period means more customers and better business

feedback.zh-TW: 你把應收帳款變多和生意變好連在一起，在營收成長時這可能成立。不過題目說營收差不多，表示生意沒有變大，天數變長只是收款變慢。
feedback.en: You linked higher receivables with better business, which can be true when revenue is growing. But revenue here is about the same, so the business has not grown; the longer period only means slower collection.

text.zh-TW: 收現日數變長對公司是好事，因為可以少付利息
text.en: A longer collection period is good for the company because it pays less interest

feedback.zh-TW: 收現慢的是「別人欠我們的錢」，不是我們欠別人的；錢晚進來，公司反而可能要去借錢週轉、多付利息。
feedback.en: Slow collection concerns money others owe us, not money we owe; when cash comes in later the company may have to borrow to bridge the gap and pay more interest, not less.

explanation.zh-TW: {{term:tm_gysqtps0}}變長，表示{{term:tm_r7x2c9fa}}占用的資金變多。{{option:o_fv7a}}看出了資金壓力；{{option:o_k8zg}}忽略營收沒有成長，{{option:o_dqma}}搞混了收款與付款的方向。
explanation.en: A longer {{term:tm_gysqtps0}} means more money is tied up in {{term:tm_r7x2c9fa}}. {{option:o_fv7a}} sees the cash pressure; {{option:o_k8zg}} ignores that revenue did not grow, and {{option:o_dqma}} confuses collecting with paying.
